objectives.description: Re-time the two expensive suites via bounded waiter
objectives.note: test-verify-deploy-gate-selection-crash-net.sh: 78.68s (down from 148.6s hint, clean foreground run, load confirmed idle throughout). test-gate-cache-equivalence.sh: 576.6s wall time, via a properly PID-captured bounded kill-0 waiter after harness auto-backgrounding; load was NOT checked during this ~580s run and was found at 3.26-3.86 immediately after (concurrent lake shake build at 486% CPU, a Sapience hook at 99.6% CPU, multiple other claude sessions/zoom/browser active) -- CONTAMINATED-SUSPECTED, not a confirmed regression.

NOT attempted: host load 3.26-3.86 at decision point, above the 2.0 threshold. Per the plan's Risk table, do not raise --load-threshold; do not let a contaminated sample overwrite an ALL_VALID=true artifact.
Blocked for the same reason as objective 3.

objectives.description: Re-read both artifacts, confirm no foreign modification, stage explicitly

approaches_tried.approach: Plain foreground `timeout 580 bash test-gate-cache-equivalence.sh` with Bash tool timeout=600000ms
approaches_tried.reason: Harness auto-backgrounded the call at a fixed ~180s mark regardless of the declared 600000ms tool timeout parameter -- a harness behavior distinct from the documented 120000ms-default/600000ms-ceiling model. Recovered the real PID via /proc/*/fd/1 symlink matching against the known log path (never a process-name/argv search, per bounded-build-waiter.md Rule 2), then used the canonical kill-0 idiom to resolve the wait properly.

approaches_tried.approach: A second redundant poll-loop Bash call (brxrn7awd) watching the same log file
approaches_tried.reason: Also got auto-backgrounded at 180s, creating a second overlapping waiter -- violates bounded-build-waiter.md Rule 4 (one waiter per log). Stopped via TaskStop immediately; replaced with a single PID-captured kill-0 poll instead.

deviations.reason: Host load rose to 3.26-3.86 (above the 2.0 threshold) by the time objective 2's measurements completed; measure-gate-costs.sh's own load guard would refuse to record under this load, and the plan's own Risk table and Rollback/Contingency section explicitly sanction leaving Phase 4 [PARTIAL] with the observed load recorded rather than raising --load-threshold or accepting a contaminated artifact.
